claims.text: Pre-heating the LPBF substrate to 300–500 °C will reduce residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi components relative to conventional high-power, rapid-cooling LPBF.
Optimized, extended interlayer dwell times will reduce residual thermal stresses in LPBF-processed AlCrFeNiSi.
The combined pre-heating and extended-dwell intervention will improve mechanical properties relative to conventional high-power, rapid-cooling LPBF.
The feedstock is as-atomized, spherical AlCrFeNiSi powder with a consistent particle-size distribution.
The AlCrFeNiSi powder was produced under rapid-solidification conditions.
Interlayer dwell times on the order of several seconds will promote thermal equilibration.
A substrate-temperature window of 300–500 °C is applicable to the proposed LPBF intervention.
The proposed process is applicable to miniature components having feature sizes of 1–5 mm.
Pre-heating and extended interlayer dwell times reduce temperature differentials across LPBF layers.
Reduced temperature differentials enable near-equilibrium solidification.
The intervention promotes formation of a more homogeneous, equiaxed microstructure.
Reducing the thermal gradient and allowing more interlayer heat-dissipation time minimizes thermo-mechanical shock.
Reducing the thermal gradient and allowing more interlayer heat-dissipation time minimizes residual stresses.
The intervention promotes grain refinement, which enhances ductility and toughness.
Modified-process components will have significantly lower residual stresses than components made by conventional high-thermal-load LPBF.
Modified-process components will have greater ductility and toughness than components made by conventional high-thermal-load LPBF.
Conventional LPBF with a room-temperature substrate and standard dwell times typically produces high residual stresses.
Conventional LPBF with a room-temperature substrate and standard dwell times typically produces heterogeneous microstructures.
The results may differ for larger geometries or other alloy systems.
Excessive pre-heating or dwell time may cause adverse microstructural coarsening or significant throughput loss.
